answer: Anyone can insure an identity against clonehood at a market rate, and when the identity is proved to be a clone the insurer pays out of its own reserve, which turns detection into a revenue stream for whoever performs it. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. Frame it as a jade on the vault, collected by the juniper: the farm pays a jade that grows with the size of its cluster, and the juniper is the party that profits from the farm being found out. Because the premium scales with the size of the correlated funding cluster.
